name: plan_three_waypoints
description: Three-skill plan: visit three markers in sequence -- (1.0, 0.0), then (1.0, 1.0), then (0.0, 1.0) -- and hold. Each skill starts only after the previous goal has been reached, so the plan is a chain of subgoals rather than a single long velocity command.
notes: min_path_length_m derivation: the three goals are the first three corners of a unit square, so a base that visits all three accumulates 1.0 + 1.0 + 1.0 = 3.0 m of travel; the gate requires 2.0 m, which is the same 50% margin the waypoint_square scenario uses for the same reason (start-up transient and the deceleration into each tolerance). The route is NOT closed -- unlike waypoint_square, which returns to the origin -- so net displacement is meaningful here, but it is deliberately not used as the gate, because a robot that reached the third goal by a different route would still have satisfied the plan. min_plan_skills_completed = 4 counts the three navigation skills and the trailing stationary hold. min_plan_waypoints_reached = 3 requires arrival at all three markers. max_final_goal_distance_m = 0.25 m is measured at the moment of arrival at the third goal, whose own tolerance is 0.15 m.
